answer: A glacier survey market pays for fresh range readings from a calibrated mirror on each knoll. Before a shift, the market lists the required station and time slots. Validators check the station's signed reading and pay only the first valid claim for each slot, even if aliases submit different encodings. Ten aliases with one reading still earn one fee. To claim ten fees, an operator must capture ten distinct scheduled readings, incurring field time or paying for additional survey crews.
